Barnaby was a big, floppy dog.
His job was to watch the back yard.
Every morning at eight o’clock, Arthur opened the door.
Barnaby ran out onto the green grass.
He sniffed the cool air.
Pip the grey squirrel sat on a tree branch.
"Woof!" barked Barnaby.
Pip held a brown nut in his paws.
"I am in my tree!" Pip said.
Pip dropped the nut to the grass.
Thud!
The nut hit the ground near Barnaby’s paws.
Barnaby picked up the nut with his mouth.
He set the nut by the tree.
Barnaby walked around the yard.
He checked under the shed.
He checked the big red hose.
Barnaby pushed three brown leaves into a pile.
Pip leaped from the tree to the fence.
Pip ran down the fence to the grass.
"Why do you push the leaves?" Pip asked.
"To keep the yard clean," Barnaby said.
Pip grabbed a dry yellow leaf.
He threw the leaf up into the air.
Pip landed on the grass with a bounce.
Barnaby blew air out of his nose.
Puff!
The leaf flew into the air.
The leaf landed right on Barnaby's nose.
Pip laughed.
Barnaby looked at the leaf on his nose.
His tail began to wag.
Arthur called out from the door.
"Barnaby! Come eat!"
Barnaby shook the leaf off his nose.
Barnaby looked up at the squirrel.
"See you tomorrow, Pip," Barnaby said.
"See you tomorrow, Barnaby!" Pip called back.
